ownership_reason: Only the gold forms the product and makes the overflow decision; hops 1 and 2 return early for a factor of one or zero and never multiply, hops 3 and 4 pass the pair along. The gold orders the pair itself (smaller and larger value), so no reordering of the operands above it changes what it sees, and the only product-preserving change a hop could make otherwise (negating both) maps the minimum value to itself and minus one to one, a legal product. Once the gold has returned Long.MIN_VALUE, a caller cannot tell an overflowed MIN * -1 from a legal MIN * 1 without re-deciding the pair itself. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the sibling overload FieldUtils.safeMultiply(long, int) takes exactly this step (case -1: the minimum value throws 'Multiplication overflows a long'), and TestFieldUtils.testSafeMultiplyLongInt asserts that safeMultiply(Long.MIN_VALUE, -1) throws and passes; FieldUtils.safeNegate throws for the negation of the minimum value ('@throws ArithmeticException if the value is Integer.MIN_VALUE'); FieldUtils.safeSubtract and safeAdd throw at the long range ends (testSafeSubtractLong, testSafeAddLong). The gold's javadoc promises an exception when the product is too big, and the true product of Long.MIN_VALUE and -1 is 2^63.
